judged_text: Post#cook returns raw verbatim for raw_html posts with no sanitization, and TopicEmbed.import stores external content through this path (RSS item bodies from Jobs::PollFeed, readability-extracted page HTML from TopicEmbed.import_remote), so the stored cooked field is unsanitized remote HTML that app/views/embed/best.html.erb renders with `raw post.cooked` (the diff's own spec asserts post.cooked == post.raw). Any markup in the imported source — script tags, event-handler attributes, or a href='javascript:...' on the allowed <a> tag, which readability's tags/attributes options do not filter — executes in the Discourse origin for every user viewing the imported topic and every visitor of the embedding blog: a compromised or plain-HTTP feed (feed_polling_url is fetched with open() over whatever scheme the admin entered) or any attacker-influenced HTML on the embeddable host yields stored XSS and admin-session takeover.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a `:raw_html` cook method where `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` from externally sourced HTML (RSS `i.content` in `Jobs::PollFeed`, and `Readability::Document` output in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`). The embed UI then renders this with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, and the added spec asserts `post.cooked == post.raw`, confirming no sanitization. This enables stored XSS via imported HTML (e.g., `<script>`, `href="javascript:..."`, etc.), and `imported_from` also interpolates `url` into an `<a href='#{url}'>` attribute after only a weak `^https?://` prefix check, allowing quote/attribute injection.
